issues: One centred 116px serif sentence and nothing else on the paper — it looks like a blank document
All 8 words press in with the same rhythm; the accent word is only recoloured, with no rhythmic emphasis
The 30px mono subline is faint and the digit roll is almost invisible
The last 8f fade all ink out, so when shown on its own the final frame is blank paper
changes: Recast as a letterpress proof sheet: crop marks grow in the corners, a registration target at top, a mono slug line at the bottom (texture), two centred lines of 136px serif; paper fibre noise over the sheet

Two-colour printing drives the rhythm: the ink pass presses words 4→24f leaving a gap for the accent word, then after a 6f pause the vermilion pass stamps 'one' on its own (1.38× start, a bigger press halo)
Everything on the vermilion plate (accent word, rule, the red registration ring) slides from a (9,−6)px misregistration into register within 12f — the proof marks become part of the technique
Ink runs through a deterministic uneven-inking noise filter plus a 1px deboss; each word leaves a brief press halo under it that springs back in 4–6f
Look = paper (vermilion accent); 32px subline with DigitRoll 44→60f; duration 55→80f with a 20f hold; the ink fade-out is now a FADE_OUT constant (off by default, so the last frame is a full poster)
